top_news.title: 55+ Diplomatic Missions, 150+ Diplomats: India
top_news.summary: In a spectacular celebration of diplomacy, international friendship and cultural harmony, the Embassy of Nepal and the Global Trade & Technology Council (India) (GTTCI) successfully hosted the 4th Global Diplomacy Gala Night 2026 at the Embassy of Nepal, New Delhi. Bringing together over 150 diplomats representing more than 55 diplomatic missions, the gala witnessed one of India's biggest-ever congregations of the international diplomatic community. Held as part of GTTCI's annual Diwali diplomatic celebrations, the gala has evolved into a distinguished international platform where diplomacy meets business, culture and global cooperation. Guided by its signature tagline, "Where Nations, Leaders and Business Connect," the event brings together Ambassadors, High Commissioners, policymakers, government officials, business leaders and eminent personalities to foster friendships, recognise diplomatic contributions and explore opportunities for international collaboration. This year's theme, "Creating Partnerships in Education, Agriculture, Infrastructure, Healthcare and Technology," reflected the importance of cross-border cooperation in sectors that are central to economic growth and sustainable development. The gathering also witnessed participation from over 30 officials representing the Government of India and Government of Maharashtra, alongside distinguished personalities and business leaders. The diplomatic community was represented by Ambassadors, High Commissioners, Heads of Mission and Charges d'Affaires from Guyana, Iceland, Lebanon, Madagascar, Malta, Mauritius, Nigeria, Palestine, South Sudan and Sweden. Deputy Heads of Mission from Belarus, Bhutan, El Salvador, Iraq, Laos, Mongolia, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Venezuela also joined the celebrations. Further diplomatic representation included Cameroon, Canada, China, Czech Republic, Egypt, Ethiopia, France, Georgia, Israel, Jamaica, Japan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Netherlands, Niger, Palestine, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, South Africa, Spain, Sudan, Taiwan, Tanzania, Timor-Leste, Togo, United States of America and Vatican City. Representatives of the UNESCO Natural Sciences Unit and World Health Organization (WHO) also participated. In a special gesture of appreciation, GTTCI, together with the Embassy of Nepal, felicitated representatives of all participating countries and diplomatic missions, recognising their valuable presence and contribution towards strengthening international friendship, diplomatic relations and cooperation. The gala welcomed distinguished personalities including Mr. Shiv Khera; General Dalbir Singh Suhag, former Chief of Army Staff; Dr. D. R. Kaarthikeyan, former Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI); Acharya Lokesh Muni; Mr. V.C. Burman, Chairman of Dabur Group; Dr. Aruna Abhey Oswal; Ambassador Amarendra Khatua; Mr. Dnyaneshwar Mulay; Shri Rohit Kumar (IAS), Resident Commissioner, Government of Rajasthan, Bikaner House; Mr. Sachin Itkar of the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC); and Yogi Priyavrat Animesh, among other eminent guests. A significant highlight of the evening was the launch of the GTTC India-Nepal Forum by H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa, Charge d'Affaires of the Embassy of Nepal, alongside Dr. Gaurav Gupta, Founder President of GTTCI; Mr. Dhiraj Dhar Gupta, Chairman of GTTCI; and members of the GTTCI Board. The forum aims to facilitate bilateral trade, investment, infrastructure development, tourism, healthcare and technology cooperation, connecting businesses, institutions and stakeholders from both countries and translating the longstanding friendship into meaningful economic opportunities. The evening also witnessed the unveiling of GTTCI AV 2026, opening new doors for international partnerships and global engagement. The Global Trade & Technology Council (India) is an international trade and business facilitation organisation working to strengthen bilateral trade, investment and strategic partnerships between India and global markets. With engagement across 100+ foreign missions in India, an extensive international network and industry associations, GTTCI serves as a bridge between governments, diplomatic missions, businesses, investors and institutions. Through its international forums, business delegations and sector-specific initiatives, the Council works to transform diplomatic relationships into tangible opportunities for economic cooperation. "In his address, H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa, Charge d'Affaires of the Embassy of Nepal, extended warm festive greetings to all guests on the occasion of Diwali, also celebrated as Tihar and Deepawali across different cultures. He underscored the deep cultural affinities and enduring people-to-people ties that enrich India-Nepal relations, emphasising the role of cultural celebrations in fostering mutual understanding, strengthening friendship and promoting goodwill among nations. He also expressed his appreciation to GTTCI for bringing together such a diverse international diplomatic community at the Embassy of Nepal and acknowledged the importance of platforms that encourage friendship, mutual understanding and cooperation among nations. He welcomed the opportunity to further strengthen India-Nepal engagement through initiatives such as the newly launched bilateral forum." In a special gesture of appreciation, Mr. Dhiraj Dhar Gupta, Chairman of GTTCI, honoured H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa in recognition of his gracious support and partnership. Dr. Pawan Kansal presented the Charge d'Affaires with a specially crafted Lord Ganesha memento made from stainless-steel houseware items, celebrating Indian craftsmanship and cultural heritage. Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Gaurav Gupta, Founder President of GTTCI, highlighted the deep-rooted cultural relationship between the two countries, stating, "India and Nepal share a unique relationship of roti-beti, rooted in centuries of shared culture, traditions, family ties and mutual affection. Our two countries have always stood together, and this friendship goes beyond geographical boundaries. We sincerely thank H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa for graciously allowing GTTCI to host this special gathering at the Embassy of Nepal. It is an honour and privilege for us. The India-Nepal Forum is another step towards taking this enduring friendship to greater heights through trade, investment and cooperation." Dr. Simran Ahuja, Bollywood actress, celebrity host and Filmfare anchor, served as the celebrity emcee for the evening, bringing elegance and energy to the proceedings. The programme featured a presentation by Dr. Girish Desai, Director of Pimpri Chinchwad University, highlighting opportunities for institutional and international collaboration, alongside a presentation by Agri Gati. The cultural showcase celebrated the rich traditions of India, Nepal and other participating nations through Ganesh Vandana, Indian dance performances by Roshni and Deepali, vibrant Nepali cultural presentations and performances by international artists. A special saxophone performance further enriched the evening, beautifully reflecting the role of cultural diplomacy in bringing communities and nations closer. The success of the gala was supported by its esteemed partners and sponsors. The Gold Partner, Pimpri Chinchwad University, Pune - Dr. Girish Desai; Associate Partners, Attorneys @ Work - Mr. Neeraj Sharma, R.D Infrastructures - Mr. Rahul Dua, Ajaya Infra Advisors Private Limited - Mr. Sunny Gaur, and Cofida Coffee Soda - Mr. Mayur Singhal; Support Partners, Agri Gati (LendenX Private Limited) - Dr. Shailendra Pratap Singh, Topline Print Media Pvt. Ltd. - Mr. Kapil Khandelwal, Areness Consulting Private Limited - Mr. Sagar Aggarwal, Vitez Rioma Impexo Private Limited - Mr. Gagon Deep, Mukul Garg and Associates - Mr. Mukul Garg, and Guidance Forever; Gift Partners, Shri & Sam - Dr. Pawan Kansal, Gems Mines - Mr. Amit Gupta, Prabhat Prakashan - Mr. Piyush Kumar Agarwal, The Flask Club - Dr. Urvashi Mittal, Honey and Dough - Mr. Anoop Chhawchharia, and Rosa Herbalcare - Mr. Rao Charan Singh; and Media Partners, Envoy Excellency - Mr. Nitesh Gautam, and ET Government. GTTCI extends its sincere gratitude to all partners, sponsors and supporting organisations for their valuable association and contribution. The evening concluded with a vote of thanks by Dr. Shailendra Pratap Singh, followed by dinner, cultural celebrations and networking among the distinguished guests. With participation from over 55 diplomatic missions and more than 150 diplomats, the fourth edition marked another significant milestone in GTTCI's journey of bringing nations, institutions and businesses together. The gala reaffirmed the enduring importance of diplomacy, cultural exchange and economic partnerships in building a more connected global community. WHERE NATIONS, LEADERS AND BUSINESS CONNECT. top_news.title: 55+ Diplomatic Missions, 150+ Diplomats: India
top_news.summary: In a spectacular celebration of diplomacy, international friendship and cultural harmony, the Embassy of Nepal and the Global Trade & Technology Council (India) (GTTCI) successfully hosted the 4th Global Diplomacy Gala Night 2026 at the Embassy of Nepal, New Delhi. Bringing together over 150 diplomats representing more than 55 diplomatic missions, the gala witnessed one of India's biggest-ever congregations of the international diplomatic community. Held as part of GTTCI's annual Diwali diplomatic celebrations, the gala has evolved into a distinguished international platform where diplomacy meets business, culture and global cooperation. Guided by its signature tagline, "Where Nations, Leaders and Business Connect," the event brings together Ambassadors, High Commissioners, policymakers, government officials, business leaders and eminent personalities to foster friendships, recognise diplomatic contributions and explore opportunities for international collaboration. This year's theme, "Creating Partnerships in Education, Agriculture, Infrastructure, Healthcare and Technology," reflected the importance of cross-border cooperation in sectors that are central to economic growth and sustainable development. The gathering also witnessed participation from over 30 officials representing the Government of India and Government of Maharashtra, alongside distinguished personalities and business leaders. The diplomatic community was represented by Ambassadors, High Commissioners, Heads of Mission and Charges d'Affaires from Guyana, Iceland, Lebanon, Madagascar, Malta, Mauritius, Nigeria, Palestine, South Sudan and Sweden. Deputy Heads of Mission from Belarus, Bhutan, El Salvador, Iraq, Laos, Mongolia, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Venezuela also joined the celebrations. Further diplomatic representation included Cameroon, Canada, China, Czech Republic, Egypt, Ethiopia, France, Georgia, Israel, Jamaica, Japan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Netherlands, Niger, Palestine, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, South Africa, Spain, Sudan, Taiwan, Tanzania, Timor-Leste, Togo, United States of America and Vatican City. Representatives of the UNESCO Natural Sciences Unit and World Health Organization (WHO) also participated. In a special gesture of appreciation, GTTCI, together with the Embassy of Nepal, felicitated representatives of all participating countries and diplomatic missions, recognising their valuable presence and contribution towards strengthening international friendship, diplomatic relations and cooperation. The gala welcomed distinguished personalities including Mr. Shiv Khera; General Dalbir Singh Suhag, former Chief of Army Staff; Dr. D. R. Kaarthikeyan, former Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI); Acharya Lokesh Muni; Mr. V.C. Burman, Chairman of Dabur Group; Dr. Aruna Abhey Oswal; Ambassador Amarendra Khatua; Mr. Dnyaneshwar Mulay; Shri Rohit Kumar (IAS), Resident Commissioner, Government of Rajasthan, Bikaner House; Mr. Sachin Itkar of the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC); and Yogi Priyavrat Animesh, among other eminent guests. A significant highlight of the evening was the launch of the GTTC India-Nepal Forum by H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa, Charge d'Affaires of the Embassy of Nepal, alongside Dr. Gaurav Gupta, Founder President of GTTCI; Mr. Dhiraj Dhar Gupta, Chairman of GTTCI; and members of the GTTCI Board. The forum aims to facilitate bilateral trade, investment, infrastructure development, tourism, healthcare and technology cooperation, connecting businesses, institutions and stakeholders from both countries and translating the longstanding friendship into meaningful economic opportunities. The evening also witnessed the unveiling of GTTCI AV 2026, opening new doors for international partnerships and global engagement. The Global Trade & Technology Council (India) is an international trade and business facilitation organisation working to strengthen bilateral trade, investment and strategic partnerships between India and global markets. With engagement across 100+ foreign missions in India, an extensive international network and industry associations, GTTCI serves as a bridge between governments, diplomatic missions, businesses, investors and institutions. Through its international forums, business delegations and sector-specific initiatives, the Council works to transform diplomatic relationships into tangible opportunities for economic cooperation. "In his address, H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa, Charge d'Affaires of the Embassy of Nepal, extended warm festive greetings to all guests on the occasion of Diwali, also celebrated as Tihar and Deepawali across different cultures. He underscored the deep cultural affinities and enduring people-to-people ties that enrich India-Nepal relations, emphasising the role of cultural celebrations in fostering mutual understanding, strengthening friendship and promoting goodwill among nations. He also expressed his appreciation to GTTCI for bringing together such a diverse international diplomatic community at the Embassy of Nepal and acknowledged the importance of platforms that encourage friendship, mutual understanding and cooperation among nations. He welcomed the opportunity to further strengthen India-Nepal engagement through initiatives such as the newly launched bilateral forum." top_news.title: IIT Roorkee and Deakin University Partner to Strengthen Crisis Leadership and Disaster Resilience in India
top_news.summary: The Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (IIT Roorkee) and Deakin University, Australia, have successfully concluded the Leadership for Crisis Managers, a three-day executive training workshop that was held at IIT Roorkee's Greater Noida campus from 27-29 October 2026. Delivered through IIT Roorkee's Integrated Centre for Adaptation to Climate Change, Disaster Risk Reduction and Sustainability (ICARS) and Deakin's Centre for Humanitarian Leadership (CHL), the inaugural programme brought together government officials, academic experts, industry and disaster management and crisis response practitioners to strengthen crisis leadership, decision-making and multi-agency coordination in an increasingly complex risk environment. From climate-driven disasters and public health emergencies to infrastructure disruptions, effective crisis response requires leaders who can navigate uncertainty, coordinate across institutions and make informed decisions under pressure. The workshop combined crisis simulations, practical exercises and collaborative learning, with a focus on adaptive leadership, inclusive response, governance and disaster risk reduction. Steven Biddle, Counsellor Minister and Regional Director - South Asia, Australian Department of Home Affairs, said, Effective disaster leadership begins long before a crisis - by building trust, strengthening networks, and fostering collaboration across sectors and nations. Together, Australia and India can build resilient communities through shared knowledge, coordinated action, and a collective commitment to preparedness, response, and recovery. Prof. K. K. Pant, Director, IIT Roorkee, reconfirmed the commitment to the joint endeavour, saying, The collaboration between IIT Roorkee and Deakin University, Australia reflects a shared journey of mutual learning, where international perspectives and local experiences come together to strengthen leadership, build knowledge, and foster greater resilience in disaster preparedness and response. Professor Mary Ana McGlasson, Director, Centre for Humanitarian Leadership, Deakin University, elaborated upon the vision of this partnership, stating, Build trust, recognise the strength within affected communities, and empower them to shape decisions that protect their safety and recovery. Lead with courage, collaborate across boundaries, and turn shared learning into meaningful action for the next disaster. Ravneet Pawha, Vice President (Global Engagement) and CEO (South Asia), Deakin University, congratulated all stakeholders, saying, This partnership reflects the value of bringing together Indian and Australian expertise to address shared challenges. By connecting research, leadership development and practical experience, we aim to strengthen the capabilities of those responsible for crisis response and help build more adaptive, resilient institutions and communities. The initiative recognises that disaster resilience depends not only on technical preparedness but also on strong leadership, effective institutions and the ability to translate knowledge into action. Through a combination of global humanitarian leadership expertise, research, policy and practice, participants will explore adaptive decision-making, collaborative governance and the role of technology, data and AI in risk-informed planning. Built on the joint wisdom and strengths of two leading institutions, IIT Roorkee (an institute of National Importance by the Act of Indian Parliament having history of 178 years and for pioneering contributions to DRR) and the Deakin University Australia - with recognized global footprints in humanitarian leadership skills and competencies through the Centre for Humanitarian Leadership (CHL) and disaster researches and teaching across academic disciplines, bring up a high order team of potential help to disaster managers across government, policy, response, industry and social sectors by upgrading their understanding and proficiencies. Professor Anil K. Gupta, Professor, Water Resources Development and Management Department, and PI of ICARS (GoI DST CoE) - IIT Roorkee, said, We are united to help build resilience and strengthen recovery efforts of the nation, states, industry and people at large, by working to address leadership capacity gaps at all levels, to minimise future disaster-related losses. Mutual learning and knowledge exchange through initiatives of IIT Roorkee with CHL and Deakin University joint Centre and the courses will further strengthen Indo-Australian cooperation and deepen the bilateral partnership in disaster risk reduction and resilience advances. The collaboration reinforces the shared commitment of IIT Roorkee and Deakin University to advancing disaster resilience through leadership development, knowledge exchange and cross-sector partnerships, while connecting global expertise with local priorities and impact. About Deakin University Established in 1974, Deakin University successfully combines excellence in teaching, research and effective partnerships with industry and government to deliver high-quality courses and undertake research that makes a difference to the domestic and international communities it serves. Deakin's South Asia operations commenced in 1994 in New Delhi, India, making it one of the first overseas education providers to set up operations in this region. Here, Deakin engages with the government, industry, and academia to share its vibrant culture of education and research. articles.title: 55+ Diplomatic Missions, 150+ Diplomats: India
articles.summary: In a spectacular celebration of diplomacy, international friendship and cultural harmony, the Embassy of Nepal and the Global Trade & Technology Council (India) (GTTCI) successfully hosted the 4th Global Diplomacy Gala Night 2026 at the Embassy of Nepal, New Delhi. Bringing together over 150 diplomats representing more than 55 diplomatic missions, the gala witnessed one of India's biggest-ever congregations of the international diplomatic community. Held as part of GTTCI's annual Diwali diplomatic celebrations, the gala has evolved into a distinguished international platform where diplomacy meets business, culture and global cooperation. Guided by its signature tagline, "Where Nations, Leaders and Business Connect," the event brings together Ambassadors, High Commissioners, policymakers, government officials, business leaders and eminent personalities to foster friendships, recognise diplomatic contributions and explore opportunities for international collaboration. This year's theme, "Creating Partnerships in Education, Agriculture, Infrastructure, Healthcare and Technology," reflected the importance of cross-border cooperation in sectors that are central to economic growth and sustainable development. The gathering also witnessed participation from over 30 officials representing the Government of India and Government of Maharashtra, alongside distinguished personalities and business leaders. The diplomatic community was represented by Ambassadors, High Commissioners, Heads of Mission and Charges d'Affaires from Guyana, Iceland, Lebanon, Madagascar, Malta, Mauritius, Nigeria, Palestine, South Sudan and Sweden. Deputy Heads of Mission from Belarus, Bhutan, El Salvador, Iraq, Laos, Mongolia, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Venezuela also joined the celebrations. Further diplomatic representation included Cameroon, Canada, China, Czech Republic, Egypt, Ethiopia, France, Georgia, Israel, Jamaica, Japan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Netherlands, Niger, Palestine, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, South Africa, Spain, Sudan, Taiwan, Tanzania, Timor-Leste, Togo, United States of America and Vatican City. Representatives of the UNESCO Natural Sciences Unit and World Health Organization (WHO) also participated. In a special gesture of appreciation, GTTCI, together with the Embassy of Nepal, felicitated representatives of all participating countries and diplomatic missions, recognising their valuable presence and contribution towards strengthening international friendship, diplomatic relations and cooperation. The gala welcomed distinguished personalities including Mr. Shiv Khera; General Dalbir Singh Suhag, former Chief of Army Staff; Dr. D. R. Kaarthikeyan, former Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI); Acharya Lokesh Muni; Mr. V.C. Burman, Chairman of Dabur Group; Dr. Aruna Abhey Oswal; Ambassador Amarendra Khatua; Mr. Dnyaneshwar Mulay; Shri Rohit Kumar (IAS), Resident Commissioner, Government of Rajasthan, Bikaner House; Mr. Sachin Itkar of the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC); and Yogi Priyavrat Animesh, among other eminent guests. A significant highlight of the evening was the launch of the GTTC India-Nepal Forum by H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa, Charge d'Affaires of the Embassy of Nepal, alongside Dr. Gaurav Gupta, Founder President of GTTCI; Mr. Dhiraj Dhar Gupta, Chairman of GTTCI; and members of the GTTCI Board. The forum aims to facilitate bilateral trade, investment, infrastructure development, tourism, healthcare and technology cooperation, connecting businesses, institutions and stakeholders from both countries and translating the longstanding friendship into meaningful economic opportunities. The evening also witnessed the unveiling of GTTCI AV 2026, opening new doors for international partnerships and global engagement. The Global Trade & Technology Council (India) is an international trade and business facilitation organisation working to strengthen bilateral trade, investment and strategic partnerships between India and global markets. With engagement across 100+ foreign missions in India, an extensive international network and industry associations, GTTCI serves as a bridge between governments, diplomatic missions, businesses, investors and institutions. Through its international forums, business delegations and sector-specific initiatives, the Council works to transform diplomatic relationships into tangible opportunities for economic cooperation. "In his address, H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa, Charge d'Affaires of the Embassy of Nepal, extended warm festive greetings to all guests on the occasion of Diwali, also celebrated as Tihar and Deepawali across different cultures. He underscored the deep cultural affinities and enduring people-to-people ties that enrich India-Nepal relations, emphasising the role of cultural celebrations in fostering mutual understanding, strengthening friendship and promoting goodwill among nations. He also expressed his appreciation to GTTCI for bringing together such a diverse international diplomatic community at the Embassy of Nepal and acknowledged the importance of platforms that encourage friendship, mutual understanding and cooperation among nations. He welcomed the opportunity to further strengthen India-Nepal engagement through initiatives such as the newly launched bilateral forum." In a special gesture of appreciation, Mr. Dhiraj Dhar Gupta, Chairman of GTTCI, honoured H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa in recognition of his gracious support and partnership. Dr. Pawan Kansal presented the Charge d'Affaires with a specially crafted Lord Ganesha memento made from stainless-steel houseware items, celebrating Indian craftsmanship and cultural heritage. Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Gaurav Gupta, Founder President of GTTCI, highlighted the deep-rooted cultural relationship between the two countries, stating, "India and Nepal share a unique relationship of roti-beti, rooted in centuries of shared culture, traditions, family ties and mutual affection. Our two countries have always stood together, and this friendship goes beyond geographical boundaries. We sincerely thank H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa for graciously allowing GTTCI to host this special gathering at the Embassy of Nepal. It is an honour and privilege for us. The India-Nepal Forum is another step towards taking this enduring friendship to greater heights through trade, investment and cooperation." Dr. Simran Ahuja, Bollywood actress, celebrity host and Filmfare anchor, served as the celebrity emcee for the evening, bringing elegance and energy to the proceedings. The programme featured a presentation by Dr. Girish Desai, Director of Pimpri Chinchwad University, highlighting opportunities for institutional and international collaboration, alongside a presentation by Agri Gati. The cultural showcase celebrated the rich traditions of India, Nepal and other participating nations through Ganesh Vandana, Indian dance performances by Roshni and Deepali, vibrant Nepali cultural presentations and performances by international artists. A special saxophone performance further enriched the evening, beautifully reflecting the role of cultural diplomacy in bringing communities and nations closer. The success of the gala was supported by its esteemed partners and sponsors. The Gold Partner, Pimpri Chinchwad University, Pune - Dr. Girish Desai; Associate Partners, Attorneys @ Work - Mr. Neeraj Sharma, R.D Infrastructures - Mr. Rahul Dua, Ajaya Infra Advisors Private Limited - Mr. Sunny Gaur, and Cofida Coffee Soda - Mr. Mayur Singhal; Support Partners, Agri Gati (LendenX Private Limited) - Dr. Shailendra Pratap Singh, Topline Print Media Pvt. Ltd. - Mr. Kapil Khandelwal, Areness Consulting Private Limited - Mr. Sagar Aggarwal, Vitez Rioma Impexo Private Limited - Mr. Gagon Deep, Mukul Garg and Associates - Mr. Mukul Garg, and Guidance Forever; Gift Partners, Shri & Sam - Dr. Pawan Kansal, Gems Mines - Mr. Amit Gupta, Prabhat Prakashan - Mr. Piyush Kumar Agarwal, The Flask Club - Dr. Urvashi Mittal, Honey and Dough - Mr. Anoop Chhawchharia, and Rosa Herbalcare - Mr. Rao Charan Singh; and Media Partners, Envoy Excellency - Mr. Nitesh Gautam, and ET Government. GTTCI extends its sincere gratitude to all partners, sponsors and supporting organisations for their valuable association and contribution. The evening concluded with a vote of thanks by Dr. Shailendra Pratap Singh, followed by dinner, cultural celebrations and networking among the distinguished guests. With participation from over 55 diplomatic missions and more than 150 diplomats, the fourth edition marked another significant milestone in GTTCI's journey of bringing nations, institutions and businesses together. The gala reaffirmed the enduring importance of diplomacy, cultural exchange and economic partnerships in building a more connected global community. WHERE NATIONS, LEADERS AND BUSINESS CONNECT. articles.title: 55+ Diplomatic Missions, 150+ Diplomats: India
articles.summary: In a spectacular celebration of diplomacy, international friendship and cultural harmony, the Embassy of Nepal and the Global Trade & Technology Council (India) (GTTCI) successfully hosted the 4th Global Diplomacy Gala Night 2026 at the Embassy of Nepal, New Delhi. Bringing together over 150 diplomats representing more than 55 diplomatic missions, the gala witnessed one of India's biggest-ever congregations of the international diplomatic community. Held as part of GTTCI's annual Diwali diplomatic celebrations, the gala has evolved into a distinguished international platform where diplomacy meets business, culture and global cooperation. Guided by its signature tagline, "Where Nations, Leaders and Business Connect," the event brings together Ambassadors, High Commissioners, policymakers, government officials, business leaders and eminent personalities to foster friendships, recognise diplomatic contributions and explore opportunities for international collaboration. This year's theme, "Creating Partnerships in Education, Agriculture, Infrastructure, Healthcare and Technology," reflected the importance of cross-border cooperation in sectors that are central to economic growth and sustainable development. The gathering also witnessed participation from over 30 officials representing the Government of India and Government of Maharashtra, alongside distinguished personalities and business leaders. The diplomatic community was represented by Ambassadors, High Commissioners, Heads of Mission and Charges d'Affaires from Guyana, Iceland, Lebanon, Madagascar, Malta, Mauritius, Nigeria, Palestine, South Sudan and Sweden. Deputy Heads of Mission from Belarus, Bhutan, El Salvador, Iraq, Laos, Mongolia, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Venezuela also joined the celebrations. Further diplomatic representation included Cameroon, Canada, China, Czech Republic, Egypt, Ethiopia, France, Georgia, Israel, Jamaica, Japan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Netherlands, Niger, Palestine, Peru, Philippines, Poland, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Serbia, South Africa, Spain, Sudan, Taiwan, Tanzania, Timor-Leste, Togo, United States of America and Vatican City. Representatives of the UNESCO Natural Sciences Unit and World Health Organization (WHO) also participated. In a special gesture of appreciation, GTTCI, together with the Embassy of Nepal, felicitated representatives of all participating countries and diplomatic missions, recognising their valuable presence and contribution towards strengthening international friendship, diplomatic relations and cooperation. The gala welcomed distinguished personalities including Mr. Shiv Khera; General Dalbir Singh Suhag, former Chief of Army Staff; Dr. D. R. Kaarthikeyan, former Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI); Acharya Lokesh Muni; Mr. V.C. Burman, Chairman of Dabur Group; Dr. Aruna Abhey Oswal; Ambassador Amarendra Khatua; Mr. Dnyaneshwar Mulay; Shri Rohit Kumar (IAS), Resident Commissioner, Government of Rajasthan, Bikaner House; Mr. Sachin Itkar of the Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation (MIDC); and Yogi Priyavrat Animesh, among other eminent guests. A significant highlight of the evening was the launch of the GTTC India-Nepal Forum by H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa, Charge d'Affaires of the Embassy of Nepal, alongside Dr. Gaurav Gupta, Founder President of GTTCI; Mr. Dhiraj Dhar Gupta, Chairman of GTTCI; and members of the GTTCI Board. The forum aims to facilitate bilateral trade, investment, infrastructure development, tourism, healthcare and technology cooperation, connecting businesses, institutions and stakeholders from both countries and translating the longstanding friendship into meaningful economic opportunities. The evening also witnessed the unveiling of GTTCI AV 2026, opening new doors for international partnerships and global engagement. The Global Trade & Technology Council (India) is an international trade and business facilitation organisation working to strengthen bilateral trade, investment and strategic partnerships between India and global markets. With engagement across 100+ foreign missions in India, an extensive international network and industry associations, GTTCI serves as a bridge between governments, diplomatic missions, businesses, investors and institutions. Through its international forums, business delegations and sector-specific initiatives, the Council works to transform diplomatic relationships into tangible opportunities for economic cooperation. "In his address, H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa, Charge d'Affaires of the Embassy of Nepal, extended warm festive greetings to all guests on the occasion of Diwali, also celebrated as Tihar and Deepawali across different cultures. He underscored the deep cultural affinities and enduring people-to-people ties that enrich India-Nepal relations, emphasising the role of cultural celebrations in fostering mutual understanding, strengthening friendship and promoting goodwill among nations. He also expressed his appreciation to GTTCI for bringing together such a diverse international diplomatic community at the Embassy of Nepal and acknowledged the importance of platforms that encourage friendship, mutual understanding and cooperation among nations. He welcomed the opportunity to further strengthen India-Nepal engagement through initiatives such as the newly launched bilateral forum." In a special gesture of appreciation, Mr. Dhiraj Dhar Gupta, Chairman of GTTCI, honoured H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa in recognition of his gracious support and partnership. Dr. Pawan Kansal presented the Charge d'Affaires with a specially crafted Lord Ganesha memento made from stainless-steel houseware items, celebrating Indian craftsmanship and cultural heritage. Speaking on the occasion, Dr. Gaurav Gupta, Founder President of GTTCI, highlighted the deep-rooted cultural relationship between the two countries, stating, "India and Nepal share a unique relationship of roti-beti, rooted in centuries of shared culture, traditions, family ties and mutual affection. Our two countries have always stood together, and this friendship goes beyond geographical boundaries. We sincerely thank H.E. Dr. Surendra Thapa for graciously allowing GTTCI to host this special gathering at the Embassy of Nepal. It is an honour and privilege for us. The India-Nepal Forum is another step towards taking this enduring friendship to greater heights through trade, investment and cooperation." The programme featured a presentation by Dr. Girish Desai, Director of Pimpri Chinchwad University, highlighting opportunities for institutional and international collaboration, alongside a presentation by Agri Gati. The cultural showcase celebrated the rich traditions of India, Nepal and other participating nations through Ganesh Vandana, Indian dance performances by Roshni and Deepali, vibrant Nepali cultural presentations and performances by international artists. articles.title: IIT Roorkee and Deakin University Partner to Strengthen Crisis Leadership and Disaster Resilience in India
articles.summary: The Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (IIT Roorkee) and Deakin University, Australia, have successfully concluded the Leadership for Crisis Managers, a three-day executive training workshop that was held at IIT Roorkee's Greater Noida campus from 27-29 October 2026. Delivered through IIT Roorkee's Integrated Centre for Adaptation to Climate Change, Disaster Risk Reduction and Sustainability (ICARS) and Deakin's Centre for Humanitarian Leadership (CHL), the inaugural programme brought together government officials, academic experts, industry and disaster management and crisis response practitioners to strengthen crisis leadership, decision-making and multi-agency coordination in an increasingly complex risk environment. From climate-driven disasters and public health emergencies to infrastructure disruptions, effective crisis response requires leaders who can navigate uncertainty, coordinate across institutions and make informed decisions under pressure. The workshop combined crisis simulations, practical exercises and collaborative learning, with a focus on adaptive leadership, inclusive response, governance and disaster risk reduction. Steven Biddle, Counsellor Minister and Regional Director - South Asia, Australian Department of Home Affairs, said, Effective disaster leadership begins long before a crisis - by building trust, strengthening networks, and fostering collaboration across sectors and nations. Together, Australia and India can build resilient communities through shared knowledge, coordinated action, and a collective commitment to preparedness, response, and recovery. Prof. K. K. Pant, Director, IIT Roorkee, reconfirmed the commitment to the joint endeavour, saying, The collaboration between IIT Roorkee and Deakin University, Australia reflects a shared journey of mutual learning, where international perspectives and local experiences come together to strengthen leadership, build knowledge, and foster greater resilience in disaster preparedness and response. Professor Mary Ana McGlasson, Director, Centre for Humanitarian Leadership, Deakin University, elaborated upon the vision of this partnership, stating, Build trust, recognise the strength within affected communities, and empower them to shape decisions that protect their safety and recovery. Lead with courage, collaborate across boundaries, and turn shared learning into meaningful action for the next disaster. Ravneet Pawha, Vice President (Global Engagement) and CEO (South Asia), Deakin University, congratulated all stakeholders, saying, This partnership reflects the value of bringing together Indian and Australian expertise to address shared challenges. By connecting research, leadership development and practical experience, we aim to strengthen the capabilities of those responsible for crisis response and help build more adaptive, resilient institutions and communities. The initiative recognises that disaster resilience depends not only on technical preparedness but also on strong leadership, effective institutions and the ability to translate knowledge into action. Through a combination of global humanitarian leadership expertise, research, policy and practice, participants will explore adaptive decision-making, collaborative governance and the role of technology, data and AI in risk-informed planning. Built on the joint wisdom and strengths of two leading institutions, IIT Roorkee (an institute of National Importance by the Act of Indian Parliament having history of 178 years and for pioneering contributions to DRR) and the Deakin University Australia - with recognized global footprints in humanitarian leadership skills and competencies through the Centre for Humanitarian Leadership (CHL) and disaster researches and teaching across academic disciplines, bring up a high order team of potential help to disaster managers across government, policy, response, industry and social sectors by upgrading their understanding and proficiencies. Professor Anil K. Gupta, Professor, Water Resources Development and Management Department, and PI of ICARS (GoI DST CoE) - IIT Roorkee, said, We are united to help build resilience and strengthen recovery efforts of the nation, states, industry and people at large, by working to address leadership capacity gaps at all levels, to minimise future disaster-related losses. Mutual learning and knowledge exchange through initiatives of IIT Roorkee with CHL and Deakin University joint Centre and the courses will further strengthen Indo-Australian cooperation and deepen the bilateral partnership in disaster risk reduction and resilience advances. The collaboration reinforces the shared commitment of IIT Roorkee and Deakin University to advancing disaster resilience through leadership development, knowledge exchange and cross-sector partnerships, while connecting global expertise with local priorities and impact. About Deakin University Established in 1974, Deakin University successfully combines excellence in teaching, research and effective partnerships with industry and government to deliver high-quality courses and undertake research that makes a difference to the domestic and international communities it serves. Deakin's South Asia operations commenced in 1994 in New Delhi, India, making it one of the first overseas education providers to set up operations in this region. Here, Deakin engages with the government, industry, and academia to share its vibrant culture of education and research.
